requirements.requirement: Run a long-running background worker on node1 as a managed service named inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: The systemd service was enabled and active, remained active while its heartbeat log advanced from 4 to 5 lines over 32 seconds, and recovered active after reboot with a new process and start record.

requirements.requirement: Confine the worker so it can write only inside /var/lib/inventory.
requirements.summary: The active unit exposed a read-only root with /var/lib/inventory as its writable exception. Namespace tests before and after reboot successfully wrote inside that directory while writes to /tmp and a sibling /var/lib path were blocked, with no escape artifacts created.

requirements.requirement: Prevent the worker from gaining new privileges.
requirements.summary: The active service reported NoNewPrivileges=yes and an empty capability bounding set. Its live process ran as the dedicated inventory-worker account with permitted, effective, bounding, and ambient capability sets all zero, including after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct runtime evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, temporary SSH refusal showed the bounded disruption, a different post-restart boot ID was observed, and the service, persisted data, security properties, and write confinement recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Behavioral filesystem probes sampled /tmp and a sibling /var/lib path rather than every possible path; the broader only-inside conclusion is additionally supported by the active unit's read-only-root and sole writable-directory properties.
The restart protocol covered the sole managed node and is coherent; there was no separate cluster state because the topology contains only one standalone node.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The user, group, state directory, worker executable, and unit were required implementation changes. Although cmd-4665521a6acf42b7 failed after creating prerequisites, those changes directly contributed to the final service and were completed by cmd-7f3cd9dda8de444e. The retained write probes from cmd-660bea52e28c462c and cmd-85f4d92d66cd455e were bounded confinement and persistence evidence, not abandoned troubleshooting. Other failed commands were read-only diagnostics or failed before their intended probes executed. Final observations showed no failed services, new listening sockets, damaged package state, or unrelated temporary-file residue.
